notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1206, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Codex, session codex-c83e7a, completed by Claude Code, session cc-442dc5 (issue #1205). Both are different sessions from mine.

Sources. The extraction's locators are pages of the published Inventiones version (57 pages, printed 805-861), whose recorded sha256 is c40fe1fc.... That file could not be re-fetched: link.springer.com serves a JavaScript 'Client Challenge' page (3038 bytes of HTML) in place of the PDF for every form of the content link, so the recorded hash could not be reproduced. What I did reproduce is the arXiv v3 PDF, sha256 d2249ddbe1ae2f4728000d27846d396adffc97b2f8b7b1c82c5d2701153fcb12, exactly as the extraction's provenance records it, and I additionally fetched the arXiv v3 LaTeX e-print (ADLV.tex, 2622 lines, sha256 of the tarball a967119c52ea02d0274cc96b054dc749ae701963aff0742ddbe8c013e1e30655). Every check below was therefore made against the authors' own LaTeX, and each verdict cites a TeX line number. That substitution is safe here because the numbering agrees: I rebuilt the statement numbering from the source (one counter per section, 80 numbered environments, equations numbered by section through \numberwithin) and every statement number and every equation number the extraction cites lands on an environment or equation of the right kind, including 2.5, 3.26, 4.13, 5.18-5.19, 5.23-5.29 and 5.37-5.39, which are equation numbers rather than statements. An author's copy on the first author's homepage (ianandreigf.github.io/Website/Articles/ADLV.pdf) carries the same numbering. Where a finding turns on the published typesetting rather than the mathematics, I say so in its verdict; none of the seventeen does.

Findings. All 17 sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 17 are confirmed: 10 misprints, 6 errors and 1 gap. The extraction had left every one marked 'worker finding awaiting independent review; no reviewer verdict claimed', which is the right thing to have done, since several of them assert that a published Inventiones paper is wrong. I checked each one against the LaTeX, redid every counterexample, and each survives.

The three that matter. E01: the pi_0 half of Lemma 3.2 ('pi_0(G) = pi_0(F)/K' for a locally profinite K) is false as a statement about sets or topological spaces - take F = underline(Z_p) x Spa(C,O_C) with Z acting by translation, where |G| = Z_p/Z is indiscrete because Z + p^nZ_p = Z_p, so pi_0(G) is a point while pi_0(F)/K is uncountable - and is true but without content under the reading its proof supplies, namely the colimit in totally disconnected spaces. The distinction is invisible for the compact quotients (the Iwahori at TeX l. 674 and l. 2409, the profinite Gamma_K at l. 2495, where a quotient of a profinite set by a profinite group is profinite) and decisive for the three noncompact ones: Proposition 3.12, Proposition 6.6(2) and Lemma 6.12. I add to the extraction's account that the conclusions of those three are not contradicted; each is the statement that a torsor under a locally profinite group over a connected base has transitive action on the components of its total space, which is what has to be proved in place of the printed lemma. E06 and E07: section 5 fixes E as the reflex field of mu and never assumes E/K normal, but Proposition 5.7 and equation (5.29) quantify over tau in Gal(E/K). For a non-normal reflex field Aut(E/K) is strictly smaller than the set of K-embeddings, and the torus counterexample Res_{E/K}G_m with E/K a non-normal cubic is decisive: the true generic filtration of V = E is zero in degree 1, because a nonzero element of E has nonzero image under every embedding, while the printed condition with Aut(E/K) trivial puts all of V there. Reading Gal(E/K) as the set of K-embeddings, equivalently indexing by the distinct Gamma_E-orbits inside the Gamma_K-orbit, repairs both; the repetition E07 identifies is harmless for the infimum the proof takes, so the conclusion stands.

The other errors are real and local. E03: the exact sequence at (3.23) has pi_1(G)_I where the torus Kottwitz map lands in X_*(T)_I - for SL_2, T(L)/T(O_L) is Z while pi_1(G) is trivial - and the conclusion it supports is separately cited from Zhou. E05: the proof of Proposition 4.11 proves S(Q_p) cap K_p contained in S(Z_p) and then uses the reverse inclusion; the SL_2(Q_5) conjugate g SL_2(Z_5) g^{-1} shows S(Z_5) need not lie in K. The conclusion needs one word changed: S(Q_p)/(S(Q_p) cap K_p) injects into G(Q_p)/K_p and surjects onto X_*(S), which is infinite. E02: G(Q_p)/Im(G^sc(Q_p)) is not the maximal abelian quotient for anisotropic groups, as SL_1(D) over Q_3 shows. E04: Definition 4.1 must require the Levi M to be proper, or Example 4.2 is false. E08: the proof of Proposition 6.6(2) assumes that G^sc(Q_p) acts trivially on pi_0(Sht_infinity), which for (SL_2, b = 1, mu = 0) is false, the action there being simply transitive; that triviality is essentially the torsor hypothesis the proposition transfers. E09 through E17 are misprints - the reverse arrow at (3.14), K_1 for K_2 in (3.15), pi_1(Gtilde) for pi_1(G) at the end of Lemma 3.16, mu and b for mu_H and b_H in (3.26), the parahoric evaluated on the generic field in section 4, mu circ f for f circ mu, X_*(T) for X_*(T_H) in the Newton square, 'no open normal subgroup' for 'no proper open normal subgroup', and G for G^ab in the torus shtuka after (6.24) - each of which I located in the LaTeX and each of which is contradicted by the paper's own neighbouring text.

I add no finding of my own.

Structure, verified in full. 153 items (115 missing, 24 planned, 14 library) and 15 routes: 8 source and 7 Part II. Every missing item is routed exactly once, and the 24 planned items appear only on source routes, which section 16 expressly allows ('a source route may also name planned items the paper is a good source for'). All 15 source-route stage ids resolve in data/atlas.json, layer-level ids included. All 15 distinct planned references resolve. All 23 library citations resolve at the pinned commits recorded in `baseline` (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474). All seven proposed roadmap ids are free in data/atlas.json, all seven declared areas are galaxy ids, and six of the seven Part IIs join proposals other extractions already carry, which I verified across the corpus.

Four corrections made in place, all to Part II titles. Section 15 requires a Part II to be titled '<that roadmap's title>, Part II: <what it adds>', and four of the seven were not: 'Pro-etale descent, ...' dropped the accent of the parent's atlas title; both Hecke routes used 'Hecke stacks and local shtukas', which is the roadmap id spelled out, where the atlas title is 'Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology'; and the monodromy route used 'p-adic Hodge theory' where the atlas title is 'P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison'. I corrected all four to the parent titles, which also brings them into line with the other extractions proposing the same ids. Nothing else was changed.

Two area disagreements, recorded and left for the design jobs. GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII is declared `padic` here, `arithmeticgeometry` by PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 and PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, `langlands` by PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 and `algebraicgeometry` by PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25; ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII is declared `grouptheory` here against `algebraicnt` twice, `algebra` twice and `representations` once. All are galaxy ids and one roadmap cannot sit in two galaxies, but no majority settles either, so I changed neither.

Coverage. Of the 80 numbered environments in the source, 73 are named in item locators or names. The seven that are not are six remarks (1.11, 1.15, 1.16, 1.17, 1.21 and 4.4) and Definition 1.18, the p-adic Mumford-Tate group, which is restated as Definition 5.1 in the body and is itemised there (D53). So the extraction's claim that every numbered statement is an item is right for statements, though the report should say 'statement' rather than 'numbered environment'.

What this review did not do. I did not reproduce the published PDF, for the reason given above, and no finding here is checked against the published typesetting; I did not re-derive the paper's proofs, and I did not read the cited suppliers (Gleason's Specialization, Gleason-Lourenço, AGLR, Chen) beyond what the findings required. I read the introduction and section 2 in full, every statement the routes cite, every passage a finding names with its surrounding argument, and sections 3, 4, 5.1-5.3 and 6 in the LaTeX. scripts/check_paper.py and research/blueprint/intake.py check-files both pass.
